subtasks.title: Render the friendly invalid-link page for ScoutSetPasswordController::guardUser() failures
subtasks.approach: guardUser() currently calls abort_if/abort_unless(403) three times, which surfaces Laravel's bare 403. Replace each with a throw of Illuminate\Http\Exceptions\HttpResponseException wrapping response()->view('auth.scout.invalid-link', [...], 403). HttpResponseException DOES pass through Illuminate\Foundation\Exceptions\Handler::render(), whose match arm `$e instanceof HttpResponseException => $e->getResponse()` returns the prepared response verbatim (it is not re-rendered, not mapped by prepareException(), and is in $internalDontReport so it is not logged) - review lanes A and B corrected an earlier, inaccurate 'bypasses the handler' phrasing here. Critically it lets guardUser() keep its `void` return type so show() and update() keep their declared `View` return types unchanged (an additive change, not a signature change). Pass a new OPTIONAL $reason to the view: 'used' for the already-verified one-shot case, 'ineligible' for the missing-org_id and missing-clarity-scout-permission cases. In the Blade template, read it as ($reason ?? null) and keep the existing $expired boolean branch fully intact, so ValidateScoutSignedUrl (which passes only $expired) needs no edit and its behaviour is untouched. PRESERVE THE EXISTING GUARD ORDER: setPermissionsTeamId($user->org_id) sits between the org_id guard and the permission guard, so the org_id guard must still short-circuit first or the permission check would evaluate against the wrong permissions team.

intended_diffs.app/Http/Controllers/Auth/ScoutSetPasswo: Import Illuminate\Http\Exceptions\HttpResponseException. Add a small private helper (e.g. rejectWith(string $reason): never) that throws HttpResponseException(response()->view('auth.scout.invalid-link', ['expired' => false, 'reason' => $reason], 403)). In guardUser(): if ($user->hasVerifiedEmail()) rejectWith('used'); if (! $user->org_id) rejectWith('ineligible'); setPermissionsTeamId($user->org_id); if (! $user->hasPermissionTo('clarity-scout')) rejectWith('ineligible'). Keep the existing one-shot explanatory comment. No change to the authorization CONDITIONS - only to how a failure is rendered.
Compute $reason = $reason ?? null at the top. Extend the <title> and the h1/p copy with two new branches ahead of the existing $expired branch: reason==='used' -> 'You have already set your password' + guidance to open Clarity Scout and sign in normally, or ask an admin to resend if they cannot get in; reason==='ineligible' -> 'This account cannot use Clarity Scout' + guidance to ask an admin to check the Scout Users setup. Leave the $expired and default-invalid branches' TEXT as they are. Precise post-review statement (lane A): the middleware-path output is byte-identical EXCEPT for added leading whitespace inside <h1>, because the new @if wrapper indents it; the asserted substrings stay contiguous so DEV-2246's tests remain green.
intended_diffs.tests/Feature/Http/Controllers/Auth/Scou: TDD: first extend the existing already-verified guard test to assert the friendly page content (see() the new 'already set your password' copy) and assert it does NOT show Laravel's bare 403; confirm RED. Add coverage for the missing-org_id and missing-clarity-scout-permission guards asserting the 'ineligible' copy, on both the GET show and POST update routes. Follow the file's existing conventions: #[Group('clarity-scout')] and the makeScannerUser() helper. Do NOT weaken the DEV-2246 signature tests - they must stay green.
